signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 195.12, reflecting an extreme G10 performance spread of 2.168% as JPY outperformance (+1.234%) collides with CHF weakness (-0.934%). Despite a 100bp carry advantage for the JPY (TONA 0.98% vs SARON -0.05%), the pair remains bid as US-Iran war tensions redraw energy maps and drive defensive flows. JPY COT LF net short -124,575 shows a crowded carry community currently under pressure from safe-haven bidding, while the JPY ESI at +16.1 confirms strong data outperformance supporting the yen. The cross is caught between structural carry-favoring JPY and the escalating Middle East conflict that traditionally favors CHF in acute risk-off regimes. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a rotation from JPY back into CHF as the primary safe haven.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Vol Complacency + Geopolitics
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.40 trades below its SMA20 (161.43) and SMA50 (161.20), testing the SMA200 at 158.05. The options market signals extreme caution with a 25d RR of -2.30, the strongest put skew in G10, as traders pay a premium for downside protection against a yen rally. Despite this, the VRP is negative at -1.2% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.4%), suggesting a dangerous complacency in the volatility surface relative to realized movement. The 275bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98%) continues to support the pair, but escalating Middle East tensions pose a high-impact threat to carry stability. Risk: A daily close below the SMA200 (158.05) triggers an accelerated unwind of the -124k COT spec short.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Vol Risk Premium + Real Rates
signals.text: GBP/USD holds at 1.3448, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3365-1.3407), marking a technically bullish posture. The options market is pricing in significant event risk ahead of US NFP with a +4.9% VRP (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.1%), the highest volatility premium across major pairs. Speculative positioning is heavily net long (+36,661), leaving the pair vulnerable to a long-unwind if US data surprises to the upside. The real rate differential remains restrictive for both, but the BoE real rate of +0.93% trails the Fed's +1.56%, limiting the long-term upside potential of the SONIA-SOFR -9bp carry advantage. Risk: US NFP beat drives 10Y yields higher, forcing a test of the 1.3365 SMA50 support.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + RBA Stance
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7037, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a period of 1.45% monthly gains. A sharp divergence has emerged as retail sentiment hits 73% short (contrarian bullish) while COT speculators remain net long (+23,616). The 71bp OIS carry advantage (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%) supports the AUD, yet the AUD ESI at -11.1 suggests the domestic data trend is starting to miss expectations. This setup creates an asymmetric risk profile ahead of the August 11 RBA meeting where a hold is expected despite the hawkish retail fade. Risk: RBA shifts to a dovish bias, validating retail shorts and breaking the 0.6997 SMA20 support.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Correlation Break + ESI Support
signals.text: EUR/USD is flat at 1.1523, testing resistance while holding above the SMA20 (1.1450) and SMA50 (1.1477). A notable correlation break is active as EUR/USD vs EuroStoxx 50 reaches a z-score of +1.59σ (corr -0.571 vs norm -0.091), indicating the Euro is increasingly decoupling from regional equity performance. While the ECB market bias remains titled toward a hike, the -92,930 COT net short position reflects a legacy bearish view that is now challenged by a positive EUR ESI of +6.4. The +146bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs €STR 2.19%) keeps the structural bid in USD, capping EUR gains despite the improving data backdrop. Risk: ECB 10 Sep meeting downplays hike bias, realigning positioning with the nominal carry disadvantage.
